sentences.text: The front tail vertebrae of Leinkupal possess extremely well-developed transverse processes that match the vertebral body width and feature robust reinforcing ridges.
Leinkupal laticauda was named and described in 2014 by Pablo Gallina, Sebastián Apesteguía, Alejandro Haluza, and Juan Canale.
The holotype specimen MMCH-Pv 63-1 consists of a single front tail vertebra found in the Berriasian–Valanginian layers of the Bajada Colorado Formation.
The genus Leinkupal contains only one known species, Leinkupal laticauda.
Leinkupal is classified within the subfamily Diplodocinae of the family Diplodocidae.
Cladistic analysis suggests Leinkupal may be a sister species to the African genus Tornieria.
Leinkupal fossils are known from the Early Cretaceous of the Bajada Colorada Formation in the Neuquén Province of Argentina.
The deposits where Leinkupal was found represent a fluvial environment characterized by braided rivers.
Leinkupal lived between 139.1 and 132.6 million years ago during the Berriasian to Valanginian stages.
